title: refactor-terraform-vpc-module-for-private-deployments
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary:
Refactor and extend the existing Terraform VPC networking module used by Redwood Private deployments. Goal is to provide a single, well-documented module that can provision multi-AZ subnets (public/private), Internet Gateway (IGW) and NAT Gateway(s), VPC endpoints (Gateway and Interface), route tables, and flexible routing policies while preserving backward compatibility with current customer state files.

Scope and deliverables:
- Module inputs/outputs: define clear, typed variables for cidr_block(s), az_count, subnet prefixes, nat mode (single/ha/none), create_igw boolean, list of managed VPC endpoints (s3,dynamodb,ssm,ecr,logs), interface endpoint map (service->subnet_ids), DNS hostname/hosted zone toggles, tags and common naming.
- High-availability options: support both single NAT (low-cost) and per-AZ NAT Gateway or NAT EC2 options, and an experimental support flag for AWS NAT Gateway with Elastic IP pool rotation.
- Routing: generate route tables per-subnet-type with explicit route propagation for peering and transit gateways. Provide optional support for centralized routing (shared-services VPC) using route table attachments.
- Conditional resources: avoid creating endpoints or NAT when explicitly disabled. Implement resource count/for_each patterns compatible with Terraform 1.x and allow plan diffs to be predictable.
- Backwards compatibility / migration: provide import instructions and state migration strategy for existing customers; include a terraform state mv cheat sheet.
- VPC endpoint health checks: add Terraform-managed CloudWatch alarms and a small Lambda-runner (optional) to validate interface endpoint ENI reachability and health (basic) post-deploy. Also include Terraform null_resource local-exec hooks for lightweight post-apply validation (dig, curl from a bastion container).
- Testing/CI: integrate module into our terraform-module CI pipeline: unit tests with terratest, plan-only checks for drift, and a staged apply target in private-development AWS account.
- Documentation: README with examples for single-account and shared-services patterns, variable reference, outputs, upgrade notes and troubleshooting.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module passes terratest suite and CI plan checks for three AZ topologies (1/2/3 AZs).
- Migration steps documented with at least one example of state import for an existing customer VPC.
- Health check resources optional and can be toggled off for air-gapped/on-prem installs.
- No breaking changes to current module inputs unless behind a new major-version flag.
- PR merged with >2 engineering approvals and a security sign-off when security_review_required=true.

Design considerations / tradeoffs noted:
- Using per-AZ NAT Gateways increases cost but simplifies routing and improves availability. Provide recommendation defaults with cost vs availability notes.
- Interface endpoints require subnet allocation; module will optionally create dedicated endpoint subnets to avoid IP exhaustion in primary private subnets.
- Some customers use Transit Gateway; module will provide hooks (route resource blocks) but not manage Transit Gateway lifecycle.

Upgrade / migration plan (high-level):
1) Release module as v2.0 with feature flag `compat_mode = true` that preserves previous resource names and tagging.
2) In staging, run `terraform plan` against an imported existing state and document expected diffs.
3) Provide `state-move.md` with exact terraform state mv commands for common migration cases (IGW, NAT Gateway, route tables, endpoints).
4) Run canary upgrades for one internal customer account using a blue/green approach; if issues, rollback via stored state snapshot.

Health checks and verification (post-apply):
- Optional CloudWatch metrics and alarms for: endpoint status, NAT gateway availability, failed route evaluations, and unexpected route table modifications.
- A lightweight Lambda (Python) that attempts TCP handshake to endpoint ENIs and posts results to an S3 bucket; configurable retention.
- Local null_resource tests that run inside an internal bastion container to validate external egress and DNS resolution of service endpoints.

Integration points / links:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.internal/redwood/private/vpc-module-design-v2
- Reference PR for tfdx patterns: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3678
- Example deployment: gs://redwood-examples/private-vpc-examples/README.md

Operational runbook (short):
- Before apply: run terraform fmt, validate, and plan. Ensure state lock.
- After apply: run `./scripts/post-deploy-verify.sh` which exercises the null_resource checks and uploads results to S3.
- If endpoints fail health checks: check subnet route tables and security groups, then verify endpoint ENI attachments and SG rules.

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the `for_each` vs `count` decisions; I chose `for_each` for endpoints to produce stable resource addresses across changes.
- The Lambda health check is optional and defaults to disabled for on-prem deployments.
- Security team: review required for IAM roles created for the Lambda and CloudWatch alarm actions.

Requested reviewers: @infra-networking, @security, @platform-ops

2026-02-24 - Liam O'Connor: Spike completed to test for_each patterns for endpoints. Confirmed stable addresses across add/remove of endpoints. Added notes to README draft.
2026-02-28 - Neha Patel (Security): Quick review - flagged that Lambda role must use least privilege and CloudWatch logs retention should be configurable. Added security_review_required=true.

2026-03-03 - Ops: Ran terratest in the private-dev account for 2-AZ topology; uncovered race condition when creating Elastic IPs for simultaneous NAT creation — introduced create_before_destroy for NAT resources.
2026-03-07 - Liam O'Connor: Opened PR #4281 with module implementation. CI failing on terratest for 3-AZ due to IP exhaustion in endpoint subnets; added optional dedicated endpoint subnet support.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Kumar: Updated ticket with migration playbook draft and state-move examples. Requesting two engineering approvals and security sign-off before merge.
